name: α-Selinene

pubchem.title: alpha-Selinene
pubchem.description: Alpha-selinene is an isomer of selinene where the double bond in the octahydronaphthalene ring system is endocyclic (2R,4aR,8aR)-configuration.. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is a member of octahydronaphthalenes and a selinene.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Alpha-selinene is a volatile organic compound and plant metabolite belonging to the terpene family. As an isomer of selinene with a distinctive ring structure, it contributes to the complex aromas and defense mechanisms of various botanicals. People most commonly encounter it in the scents and flavors of familiar herbs, fruits, and essential oils.
consumer_summary.found_in: It is naturally found in hops, guava, and celery, and has also been identified in the essential oils of Cannabis sativa and sweet wormwood.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to alpha-selinene for its prominent role in the defense systems of plants, particularly its ability to ward off microbes and insects. The strongest evidence so far comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b) looking at its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties in botanical extracts. Scientists are actively exploring how this natural compound might be harnessed for everything from natural food preservation to novel mosquito repellents.

structure_function.statement: Alpha-selinene may support the body's natural defenses against certain bacteria and fungi.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 26 papers, including human observational and in vitro studies evaluating botanical extracts.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward alpha-selinene having antioxidant properties that may help neutralize free radicals.
structure_function.basis: This is supported by 11 papers, including human observational research.

structure_function.statement: The compound is being studied for its potential to support healthy inflammatory responses.
structure_function.basis: This is based on 3 papers, including early human observational and animal research.

structure_function.statement: Alpha-selinene may act as a natural insect repellent.
structure_function.basis: This rests on 8 papers, primarily bench and animal research.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether alpha-selinene or the plant extracts containing it might influence cellular health and tumor pathways. If this bears out, it could highlight certain dietary terpenes as supportive agents in cellular protection.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial (Oxford level 1b) administering a standardized alpha-selinene extract to measure specific biomarkers of cellular proliferation and oxidative stress over six months.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward alpha-selinene potentially playing a role in pain relief, possibly by interacting with inflammatory pathways.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A pilot human clinical trial (Oxford level 1b) evaluating the analgesic effects of a topical alpha-selinene preparation in healthy volunteers subjected to mild, induced localized pain over a two-week period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether alpha-selinene can effectively combat persistent fungal strains, such as Candida albicans, which are often resistant to conventional treatments.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized controlled trial (Oxford level 1b) testing a topical alpha-selinene formulation against a standard antifungal cream for superficial skin infections over four weeks.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) on its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties; most of the rest is animal and lab research.
